title: Information Management Systems
description: A practical course on managing information with the Microsoft Office suite: Word for documents, Excel for data and calculations, Access for databases, and PowerPoint for effective presentations. Built from Dr Nancy C. Woods's CSC 272 lecture notes (Lectures One to Thirteen), the introductory class slides and the PowerPoint tutorial.

topics.title: Introduction to Microsoft Office
topics.summary: CSC 272 teaches four Microsoft Office applications for storing data, analysing it into information and presenting it: Word (a word processor), Excel (a spreadsheet), Access (a database) and PowerPoint (presentations). Each has its own file type and its own uses.

topics.title: The Microsoft Word Environment
topics.summary: The Word 2013 window is built around the File tab, the Ribbon of tabs, groups and commands, contextual tabs and the Quick Access Toolbar. Each tab collects related tools, from Home and Insert to Mailings, Review and View, and Word offers several views of a document.
subtopics: The File tab and protecting a document
The Ribbon: tabs, groups and commands
The main tabs and contextual tabs

topics.title: Editing and Formatting Word Documents
topics.summary: Word documents are created, saved and then formatted: text formatting, alignment, line and paragraph spacing, lists and sorting; cut, copy, paste and drag and drop; find and replace; page layout; proofing tools; indents; and tables.
subtopics: Cut, copy, paste and drag and drop
Page layout, proofing, indents and tables

topics.title: Microsoft Excel Basics
topics.summary: Excel files are workbooks of worksheets made of cells, each with an address. The Excel window has an active cell, columns, rows, fill handle, name box, formula bar and sheet tabs. Students manage worksheets, enter and edit data, use autofill, and format cells and data.
subtopics: Alignment, wrap text, merge and number formats

topics.title: Excel Formulas, Functions and Charts
topics.summary: Excel formulas start with an equals sign and use the operators +, -, * and /, recalculating automatically when values change. Functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX and MIN are predefined formulas. Charts present data visually, and print preview and page setup prepare a sheet for printing.
subtopics: Print preview, printing and page setup

topics.title: Microsoft Access and Databases
topics.summary: Access is a relational database application. A database is a structured collection of related tables made of records and fields. Access has four objects: tables, queries, forms and reports. Good design follows rules such as no derived or calculated fields, smallest logical parts, descriptive and unique field names, and a primary key for every table.
subtopics: Tables: design view, data types and datasheet view
Fields, records, tables, queries and keys

topics.title: PowerPoint and Effective Presentations
topics.summary: PowerPoint builds presentations from slides with layouts and placeholders, themes and pictures. An effective presentation is planned for its purpose, audience and time, and follows design rules such as the 6 x 6 rule, high contrast and sparing animation. Views, slide show, transitions, animations and speaker notes support delivery.
subtopics: Design rules and the 6 x 6 rule
